title: Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion: One Model, Three Decoding Modes
hook: Instead of picking autoregressive or diffusion decoding, Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion trains one model to do both — plus a self-speculation mode that decodes up to 6x more tokens per forward pass.
key_points: A single model is trained with a joint AR-diffusion objective, then can switch decoding mode to fit the deployment setting and concurrency level.
The authors argue AR and diffusion are complementary: diffusion helps lookahead planning, AR supplies left-to-right linguistic priors.
In self-speculation mode, a diffusion drafter proposes tokens and an AR verifier checks them — beating multi-token prediction (MTP) on both acceptance rate and real-device speed.
Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-8B decodes up to 6x more tokens per forward pass than Qwen3-8B at comparable accuracy, for ~4x higher throughput on SPEED-Bench (SGLang, GB200).
Scales to 3B/8B/14B, with base, instruct, and vision-language variants, consistently beating prior open AR and diffusion LMs on accuracy and speed.
content_html: Most language models pick one decoding strategy — autoregressive, one token at a time, or diffusion, denoising a block at once — and stick with it. Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion trains a single model to do both, plus a third mode that combines them.
extra_html: The model is trained with a joint AR-diffusion objective, so it can switch modes to sustain high throughput across different deployment settings and concurrency levels. The authors' framing: AR and diffusion objectives are complementary rather than substitutes — diffusion improves lookahead planning, while AR supplies the left-to-right linguistic priors AR models are known for. The most notable mode is self-speculation: the model's diffusion side drafts tokens, and its own AR side verifies them, which the paper reports beats multi-token-prediction (MTP) approaches on both acceptance rate and real-device efficiency. Scaled to 3B, 8B, and 14B parameters (with base, instruct, and vision-language variants), Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-8B decodes up to 6x more tokens per forward pass than Qwen3-8B at comparable accuracy, translating to roughly 4x higher throughput on SPEED-Bench under SGLang on a GB200 GPU. From NVIDIA, arXiv, 2026-07-07.

related.title: NVIDIA Nemotron-TwoTower: A Diffusion-Based Language Model
related.hook: NVIDIA's open Nemotron-TwoTower bolts a diffusion 'denoiser' tower onto a frozen autoregressive model to fill token blocks in parallel — reportedly 2.42x faster at ~98.7% of baseline quality.

related.title: iLLaDA: Improved Large Language Diffusion Models
related.hook: An 8B language model trained from scratch with full bidirectional attention and a masked-diffusion objective — no autoregression — that holds its own against same-size autoregressive LLMs.

related.title: Speculative Decoding
related.hook: Let a small, fast model guess the next few words, then have the big model check them all in one shot. Same output, fewer slow steps.

related.title: JetSpec: Breaking the Scaling Ceiling of Speculative Decoding
related.hook: Speculative decoding stalls when bigger draft trees stop paying off. JetSpec trains a causal parallel draft head that drafts in one pass yet stays branch-consistent — hitting up to 9.64x speedup.

flashcards.prompt: What are the three decoding modes Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion unifies in one architecture?
flashcards.back_html: Autoregressive (AR), diffusion, and self-speculation — where a diffusion drafter proposes tokens and an AR verifier checks them, all within a single model trained on a joint AR-diffusion objective.

flashcards.prompt: How does self-speculation mode differ from standard multi-token prediction (MTP)?

choices.text: A diffusion drafter (not a simple MTP head) proposes tokens, verified by the model's own AR mode, beating MTP on acceptance rate and real-device speed
It skips verification entirely and trusts the drafted tokens
It requires a separate, differently-trained drafter model

flashcards.explanation_html: Self-speculation reuses the same model's diffusion capability as the drafter and its AR capability as verifier, and the authors report it outperforms MTP methods on both acceptance rate and real-device efficiency.

flashcards.prompt: Why do the authors say AR and diffusion training objectives are complementary rather than competing?
flashcards.back_html: Diffusion improves lookahead planning (seeing more of the sequence at once), while AR provides left-to-right linguistic priors — combining both in one model, rather than picking one, is what enables mode-switching.
